data: Skeleton entry for /fleet (PRD-012 v0.2 / Phase A scaffold). Builder + agency + first-flight per public sources. Specs and gallery TBD in later phases.
Vostok 1 (1961-04-12) · Yuri Gagarin — first human in space; 108-min single orbit; ejected and parachuted to Earth (capsule landed separately)
Vostok 2 (1961-08-06) · Gherman Titov — first full day in space (17 orbits); first space sickness recorded; youngest cosmonaut at 25
Vostok 3 (1962-08-11) · Andriyan Nikolayev — first simultaneous-flight dual mission with Vostok 4; 4 days / 64 orbits
Vostok 4 (1962-08-12) · Pavel Popovich — flew alongside Vostok 3; passed within 6.5 km of each other on first orbit
Vostok 5 (1963-06-14) · Valery Bykovsky — longest solo crewed spaceflight ever (4 days 23 h, still standing in 2026)
Vostok 6 (1963-06-16) · Valentina Tereshkova — first woman in space; flew alongside Vostok 5; 48 orbits

The Vostok spacecraft was the first machine to carry a human into space and bring one back, and its design is a study in doing the minimum that works. Reentry is the hardest part of coming home, so Vostok used the one shape that survives it from any angle — a sphere — which meant the automatic systems never had to point the craft precisely; it would tumble in and still come down heat-shield-heavy. The catch was that the sphere landed too hard for a person, so the cosmonaut ejected near the ground and parachuted separately, a fact hidden for years to protect the records. Crude, secretive, and completely effective, it flew six people to orbit and lost none — and its capsule-plus-service-module layout became the pattern for Soyuz, still flying today.

The spherical descent module that returned Yuri Gagarin from orbit on 1961-04-12 — the first human spaceflight. Six crewed flights between 1961 and 1963, including Valentina Tereshkova’s solo orbital mission as the first woman in space.
First human in space; first crewed orbital flight
First day in space — 17 orbits over 25 hours
First dual-flight rendezvous — flew within ~6.5 km of Vostok 4
Second half of first dual flight — first communications between two crewed spacecraft
Longest solo Earth-orbital flight — 4 days 23 hours, 81 orbits
First woman in space — Valentina Tereshkova, 48 orbits
Soviet R-7-derived launcher that put Gagarin in space — Vostok 1 (1961-04-12) and 5 more Vostok flights through 1963
Sputnik 1 (1957). Vostok 1 — Gagarin (1961). Five hundred and forty Soyuz launches from a single pad.
First Soyuz generation; Komarov's fatal flight
